english.title: Political parties - treasurer fail to return donation - unidentifiable donor

additionalkeywords.additionalkeyword: POLITICAL PARTIES ELECTIONS AND REFERENDUMS ACT 2000

english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) being the treasurer of a registered party, namely **(..SPECIFY PARTY..), in receipt of a donation from an unidentified donor falling within Section 54(1)(b) of the Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000, failed to

(A)_[return the donation to the person who transmitted the donation, namely **(..SPECIFY..)]_
(B)_[return the donation to an identifiable financial institution, namely **(..SPECIFY..), having been apparent that it provided a facility to the donor, in connection with the donation]_
(C)_[send the donation to the Commission]_

within thirty days of receiving the donation.
english.legislation:
Contrary to section 56(4) of and Schedule 20 to the
Political Parties, Elections and Referendums Act 2000.

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
Any reference to returning or sending a donation to any
person or body includes a reference to sending a payment of an equal amount to that person
or body.

other.penalty:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: One year imprisonment or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None

On the 12th March 2015 the limit on fines imposed by a Magistrates’ court was removed – as such, the potential fine on summary conviction in relation to an offence committed after this date is unlimited.
